value.value: $1,000,000,000 (Total Commitments as of the Closing Date); revolving Facility with $75,000,000 aggregate L/C Commitments; Commitment Increase option up to an aggregate of $750,000,000
value.note: verbatim: ““ Commitment ”: as to any Lender, the obligation of such Lender, if any, to make Loans and participate in Letters of Credit in an aggregate principal and/or face amount not to exceed the amount set forth under the heading “Commitment” opposite such Lender’s name on Schedule 1.1A or in the Assignment and Assumption pursuant to which such Lender became a party hereto, as the same may be changed from time to time pursuant to the terms hereof. As of the Closing Date, the amount of the Total Commitments is $1,000,000,000.”

value.value: Term Benchmark Loans: Adjusted Term SOFR + Applicable Margin; RFR Loans: Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR + Applicable Margin; ABR Loans: ABR + Applicable Margin. Adjusted Term SOFR = Term SOFR Rate + 0.10%. Applicable Margin for Term Benchmark/RFR Loans ranges 1.125%–1.75%; for ABR Loans 0.125%–0.75% (per leverage/ratings grid); default rate = otherwise applicable rate + 2%
value.note: verbatim: “(a) (i) Each Term Benchmark Loan shall bear interest for each day during each Interest Period with respect thereto at a rate per annum equal to the Adjusted Term SOFR determined for such day plus the Applicable Margin and (ii) each RFR Loan ... shall bear interest at a rate per annum equal to the Adjusted Daily Simple SOFR plus the Applicable Margin. (b) Each ABR Loan shall bear interest at a rate per annum equal to the ABR plus the Applicable Margin.”

value.value: Termination Date = fifth anniversary of the Closing Date (Closing Date: March 26, 2024), subject to extension pursuant to Section 2.18 (up to two one-year extensions)
value.note: verbatim: ““ Termination Date ”: the fifth anniversary of the Closing Date, subject to the extension thereof pursuant to Section 2.18 . ... The Borrower shall repay all outstanding Loans on the Termination Date.”

value.value: Consolidated Leverage Ratio not to exceed 4.00 to 1.00 (or 4.50 to 1.00 for any fiscal quarter during an Acquisition Step-Up Period), tested at end of each fiscal quarter for the period of four consecutive fiscal quarters, on a Pro Forma Basis
value.note: verbatim: “7.1 Financial Condition Covenant . Permit the Consolidated Leverage Ratio, calculated as at the end of any fiscal quarter for the period of four consecutive fiscal quarters of the Borrower then ended, on a Pro Forma Basis, to exceed (x) 4.00 to 1.00, or (y) 4.50 to 1.00 for any fiscal quarter during any Acquisition Step-Up Period, calculated as at the end of any fiscal quarter ending during any Acquisition Step-Up Period; provided that that there shall be no more than two Acquisition Step-Up Periods after the Closing Date and each Acquisition Step-Up Period shall be separated by at least two calendar quarters.”

value.value: Unsecured facility (no security/collateral grant except springing equal-and-ratable Lien under Section 7.3). Springing guarantee: each Domestic Subsidiary that guarantees Borrower Indebtedness (clauses (a) and (c)) of $150,000,000 or more must guarantee the Obligations within 60 days; releasable per Section 6.7(b). Section 7.3 equal-and-ratable clause: if Liens securing Indebtedness are created, the Obligations shall be secured equally and ratably
value.note: verbatim: “6.7 Subsidiary Guarantee . (a) Each Domestic Subsidiary that guarantees Indebtedness of the Borrower of the type contemplated by clauses (a) and (c) of the definition thereof in an aggregate principal amount of $150,000,000 or more will guarantee the Obligations under the Facility pursuant to documentation reasonably satisfactory to the Administrative Agent within 60 days of the incurrence of such guarantee (or such longer period as may be agreed by the Administrative Agent).”

value.value: Events of Default (Section 8.1): (a) payment default (principal when due; interest/other amounts within 5 days); (b) misrepresentation; (c)/(d) covenant defaults (Section 7 and others, 30-day cure for (d)); (e) cross-default/cross-acceleration on Indebtedness exceeding $200,000,000 in aggregate; (f) bankruptcy/insolvency (60-day for involuntary); (g) ERISA events (with Material Adverse Effect); (h) unsatisfied judgments of $200,000,000 or more (60-day period); (i) change of control – person/group beneficial owner of more than 50% of outstanding common stock. Acceleration: automatic upon Borrower bankruptcy (f)(i)/(ii); otherwise upon Required Lenders' direction. No general mandatory prepayment covenant stated; optional prepayments permitted without premium or penalty (Section 2.5); certain cash-collateralization obligations for L/C Obligations exceeding limits
value.note: verbatim: “8.1 Events of Default . If any of the following events shall occur and be continuing: (a) the Borrower shall fail to pay any principal of any Loan or Reimbursement Obligation when due ...; or ... (e) ... one or more defaults, events or conditions of the type described in clauses (i) or (ii) of this paragraph (e) shall have occurred and be continuing with respect to Indebtedness the outstanding principal amount of which exceeds in the aggregate $200,000,000; or (f) ... [bankruptcy] ...; or (h) one or more judgments or decrees shall be entered against the Borrower involving in the aggregate a liability ... of $200,000,000 or more ...; or (i) any “person” or “group” ... becomes the “beneficial owner” ... directly or indirectly, of more than 50% of the outstanding common stock of the Borrower;”

synthesis.evidence_balance: mixed — trailing/own-history cheapness and rising absolute EBITDA offset by a genuine revenue stall, goodwill write-down, and structurally harder selling environment.

bull_points.claim: The EV/EBITDA multiple sits at 8.0x (TEV/LTM), a 3rd-percentile floor of its own 38-quarter range (7.5–37.8x, median 23.4x), so the de-rating is severe relative to the name's own history — a trailing observation, not a signal by itself.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Multiples 'TEV/LTM EBITDA' Close (latest) — current multiple

bull_points.claim: Absolute EBITDA has kept rising through the de-rating — $1,148M (2021) → $1,274M (2023) → $1,311M (2025) → $1,337M LTM Mar-2026 — so the falling multiple reflects price collapse, not earnings collapse; the margin-% decline is the optical misread, absolute EBITDA is the real signal.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Income Statement (margin % + absolute EBITDA reconciler)

bull_points.claim: The business earns high returns on capital (RoCE ~19.4% LTM, up from 18.6% FY25) and remains well above its own pre-2021 base, evidencing a franchise, not a fading asset.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Financials→Ratios (Return on Capital %, multi-year columns)

bull_points.claim: Leverage is modest — net-debt/EBITDA 1.3x and interest coverage 10.1x — leaving ample capacity to service the all-senior-unsecured note stack and fund the buyback.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Net Debt $1,688M [Q1 Mar-31-2026] ÷ CIQ EBITDA $1,337M [LTM 12 months Mar-31-2026]

bull_points.claim: Management is aggressively retiring stock — share count -13.1% over ~1.8y, with $535M repurchased in Q1 2026 alone — accreting per-share value at the depressed multiple.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Gartner, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 05, 2026.rtf

bull_points.claim: Contract value — the leading subscription indicator — grew 1% YoY in Q1 2026 and 3.5% ex-U.S.-federal, an acceleration from year-end, suggesting the revenue soft-patch is federal-concentrated rather than franchise-wide.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ transcript: Gartner, Inc., Q1 2026 Earnings Call, May 05, 2026.rtf

bull_points.claim: Consensus target price mean $160.38 sits far above the ~$155.84 last close only modestly, but the guidance-delivery track record is strong (revenue actual≥floor 27/28; EPS 28/30; most recent FY25 MET), evidencing durable execution against guides.
bull_points.source_ref: CIQ Estimates→Guidance (latest guide + sign-aware delivery track-record)

bear_points.claim: Revenue growth has stalled — Q1 Mar-2026 revenue -1.5% YoY same-quarter, and FY26 consensus revenue has been cut ~8% (12m→latest) to $6,426M — a genuine top-line deceleration, not merely optics.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ Estimates→Trends (current-FY consensus path; ragged, absent lookbacks n/a)

bear_points.claim: The stock is idiosyncratically broken: -45% over 180d while the MDY benchmark was +11.7%, a -56.7% relative gap driven by a discrete 2026-02-03 earnings/Reg-FD gap-down — the market is pricing a company-specific impairment, not a sector move.
The de-rating event carried a $150M goodwill impairment tied to Digital Markets, a tangible write-down of prior capital deployed — a real signal of asset value destruction, not a timing artifact.

EBITDA margin has drifted down from a 24% 2021-22 peak to 20-21% and consensus growth is anaemic (name EBITDA growth 2% vs peer-median 7%), so the discount may be earned on a decelerating-fundamentals basis rather than a pure overshoot.
bear_points.source_ref: CIQ Comparable Analysis→Operating Statistics (name vs peer median: growth/margin/leverage/beta)

bear_points.claim: Management itself flags a structurally tougher selling environment — deferred decision-making, extended buying cycles, DOGE/federal and tariff pressure — a demand-side headwind narrated as persistent, not one-off.

business_description.value: Gartner, Inc. provides business and technology insights for decisions and performance on an organization’s mission-critical priorities in the United States, Canada, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and internationally. It operates through three segments: Insights, Conferences, and Consulting. The Research segment delivers insights through subscription services, such as access to published content, data and benchmarks, and direct access to a network of business and technology experts. The Conferences segment offers executives and teams in an organization the opportunity to learn, share, and network through its Symposium/Xpo series and peer-driven sessions, as well as conferences focused on specific business roles and topics. The Consulting segment provides technology-driven strategic initiatives, including custom analysis and on-the-ground support to senior executives. This segment also offers actionable solutions for IT-related priorities, including IT cost optimization, digital transformation, and IT sourcing optimization. Gartner, Inc. was founded in 1979 and is headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut.
